items.title: DOJ seeks emergency court order to freeze ~20,000 California mail ballots; charges 28 in 'Operation Protect the Vote'
items.summary: The Justice Department filed an emergency motion Oct 19 in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California (United States v. California, No. 2:26-cv-12025) asking a federal judge to order California and Los Angeles County to segregate ~20,000 vote-by-mail ballots from people on a federal 'likely noncitizen' list and not count them until citizenship is verified. The same day DOJ announced 'Operation Protect the Vote': 28 lawful permanent residents charged across California's four federal districts (11 arrested; DOJ says 22 cast ballots). The list was delivered to California on Oct 14 on a thumb drive with a hand-scrawled password on a sticky note, plus a 48-hour ultimatum; California refused, and DOJ sued Oct 15. Gov. Gavin Newsom accused President Trump of attempting to rig the election; DOJ says California's refusal 'hampers' prosecution. Election-law experts are skeptical of DOJ's chances, per NPR. No hearing had been scheduled as of Oct 20. 20,000 is a 'likely' figure the DOJ itself calls 'the floor.'

items.title: 613 Warren County, Iowa voters mistakenly received two absentee ballots
items.summary: Warren County auditor Kimberly Sheets announced that 613 county residents were erroneously sent two absentee ballots for the Nov. 3 general election instead of one. The ballots have been identified and flagged: only one per voter will be counted, and affected voters are being notified. Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate said safeguards ensure each voter can only have one ballot counted; neither office identified how the error occurred. Iowa's Senate race (Hinson vs. Turek) is the prediction markets' lone toss-up; in-person early voting there began Oct 14.

items.title: Prediction markets nudge toward Democrats: Senate 65% (+2 pts on the week), House 91% (+1)
items.summary: DeFi Rate's Oct 21 prediction-market tracker: Democrats 65% to win Senate control, up 2 points in 7 days (Kalshi 65.6¢, Polymarket 65¢), and 91% for the House, up 1 point (Kalshi 90.8¢, Polymarket 92¢). Kalshi's live board: Democrats favored in 18 of 35 Senate races; Texas Senate Talarico 63% vs. Paxton 37% remains the most-traded competitive race; Iowa the lone toss-up (Dem 44%); Kansas R 61%, South Carolina's Graham 83%. Markets remain more bullish on Democrats than forecast models (DDHQ and Call the Map ~56-57% Dem Senate). A Democratic sweep is priced around 62¢ on Kalshi.

items.title: RNC expands vote-protection operation: directors in 22 states, 21,500 poll workers, 179 active cases
items.summary: The RNC said Oct 19 it expanded its election-integrity operation with 15 days to Election Day: Election Integrity Directors in 22 target states, more than 21,500 poll workers (double its 2024 total), and 179 active cases across 37 states. The committee cited past outcomes including stopping New York City's attempt to let nearly 800,000 noncitizens vote and a voter-roll records initiative across 48 states, and said it is fighting for proof-of-citizenship to vote at the U.S. Supreme Court. Single-sourced: only the niche legal site Jurelist reported the new figures; no major-outlet corroboration found. Note these are the RNC's own numbers.
